author: Dominic Bisogno
title: Champlin Park football wins one battle after another - NewsBreak
text:
By Dominic Bisogno ,
2 days ago
Champlin Park football hosted rivals Anoka in a battle for the paddle to remember Oct. 4, beating the Tornadoes by one point after powerful offensive performances by quarterback Miles Felton and Preston Nelson, plus huge defensive moments from the likes of Mario Robinson, Will Ogunti, and Eric Lukes Jr.
Battle for the paddle
The night immediately turned into a back and forth between two teams determined to win. Champlin Park and Anoka scored a touchdown in each in the first quarter, the Rebels’ arriving first with a touchdown run for six yards by Nelson. An unsuccessful extra point attempt meant that Anoka led 7-6 upon scoring soon after.
The chess match continued in the second quarter, with Nelson running in another touchdown, while Felton ran in a two-point conversion and a separate touchdown of his own. Trace Fitzgerald nailed his second extra point attempt of the night, with two Anoka touchdowns, each following one of Champlin Park’s, making it 21-21 at halftime.
Anoka has had a hard year, arriving at Champlin Park High School with a 0-5 record that included narrow losses to Osseo and Andover. Their Rebel rivals have had the opposite sort of fall, going 4-1 in their first five games with a series of statement wins over the likes of St. Michael-Albertville, Andover and Blaine, only broken up by a 31-10 loss to Centennial.
Felton continued to be a threat on the run, scoring a second touchdown to start the third quarter with a blistering 61-yard carry. Anoka’s passing game continued to thrive, however, and the Tornadoes tied it up at 28-28 with six minutes left in the quarter.
Anoka recovered a fumble in the following drive to get the ball back and put Champlin Park under pressure, but junior Will Ogunti made two huge plays in that resulting drive, sacking the quarterback to force an Anoka fourth down, and then blocking the punt. Anoka got the ball back again, but a sack by Damon Torke slowed their progress once more.
The tornadoes did score four minutes into the fourth quarter, taking a 35-28 lead. Champlin Park responded with a gritty drive, finding narrow first downs when needed to set up Nelson, who dragged it over the line as the score went up to 35-35.
With the Rebels looking for a way to change the game, Lukes Jr. found the answer. The junior corner caught a pick and ran for roughly 50 yards, getting stopped only at the Anoka four yard line. Nelson ran it in from there, with an extra point making it 42-35 with one minute and 39 seconds on the clock.
Anoka went for it, plummeting down the field and eventually, after several downs of work and just three seconds on the clock, scored their touchdown in response. But, the Tornadoes went for a two point conversion, looking to win the game. The quarterback found a target and made the throw, but sophomore Robinson came up with a block, ending the game there at 42-41.
Seeing through adversity
Champlin Park’s 5-1 record has been a hard-fought one. The Rebels have now won three games by the margin of one-possession and have done so with a young group. Many of Friday’s key performers were not seniors, including Felton, Nelson, Lukes Jr., Ogunti, Robinson and Torke.
Head coach Nick Keenan told Sun Newspapers that the team had questions to answer at the start of the season, but that he has been more than happy with the response he has seen so far.
“We have a ton of junior starters, so we didn’t quite know if or what they knew about the varsity experience,” he said. “Tonight, we came in, having watched film, that this is a really good Anoka offense. We told the kids, we might have to outscore them. There were times in the game where we could’ve gotten done, but we battled back. We did it last week, we did it this week. Hopefully that’s a sign that it’s getting into their DNA a little bit. I’m so proud of them, it came down to the final play and we got it done.”
The Rebels still have areas to improve, which Keenan explained largely came down to a higher level of execution.
“Anoka had three third and longs tonight where we didn’t get off the field,” he explained. “They went on to score on all of those drives, so if we hold them there, it’s a totally different game.”
Champlin Park are nearing the end of the regular season with a lot of momentum at their backs. The Rebels will enter their last two games as favorites, likely to enter the playoffs with a 6-2 or 7-1 record, something that could give them a strong seeding and set a tone for their state hopes.
Keenan added that the coaches are starting to work on helping the players understand what is coming their way, with the possibility of new attention and new pressure when the 6A tournament kicks off.
“We’ve talked to the kids about what’s coming next, because I don’t think some of them understand what’s in front of them. They’re just young and inexperienced at this level,” he continued. “There’s a lot to think about. We just have to win out our games and we’ll get the seed we get. But, we always tell them that every week of 6A football is a tough one.”
Champlin Park will hit the road the following week, traveling to Lakeville North (1-5) on Friday, Oct. 10.
